_comment: Shared enforcement vectors. Replayed by backend/internal/policy (Go) and by the Android DPC's
enforcement engine (Kotlin). Two engines that disagree is the failure mode this file exists to
prevent, so neither side may edit it to make its own implementation pass.
'expect' is a PARTIAL DesiredState: only the keys present are asserted, and an unknown key is a
test failure rather than a silently ignored typo. Expectations are written by hand from
REQUIREMENTS.md — never generated from an implementation's output, which would assert only that
the code does what it does.

vectors.name: idle: nothing configured, nothing enforced
bedtime: inside the window suspends non-exempt apps
bedtime: leaving the window un-suspends — the state is not one-way
bedtime: the boundary minute is inside the window, the end minute is outside
bedtime: the end minute is already outside the window
bedtime: the minute before the end is still inside the window
bedtime: start equal to end is disabled, not a 24-hour lockdown
bedtime: the window survives the end of daylight saving time
quota: reaching the daily limit suspends for the rest of the local day
quota: one minute short of the limit enforces nothing
quota and bedtime together: the earlier edge is the next change
app rules: a blocked app is suspended and hidden
critical whitelist survives bedtime, an exhausted quota, an explicit block and a parent lock
youtube killswitch on: apps, dns and browser blocklist together
youtube killswitch off: the inverse restores every layer
free-installation off: a new app waits for a parent, an allowed one does not
free-installation on: new apps are inventoried, not blocked
tracking-only: measures everything, restrains nothing, still filters and hardens
tracking-only still honours an explicit parent lock
a different filtering endpoint per child is honoured verbatim
managed apps: a declared set reaches the device, sorted and unchanged
managed apps: an entry the phone could not act on is dropped, and one package keeps one version
managed apps: declaring an app is not allowing it — bedtime still suspends it
family blocklist: one list covers the family, including a package no phone reported
family blocklist: a child ALLOW is the exemption, and it does not reach that child's own BLOCK
family blocklist: the critical whitelist outranks it — a keyboard on the list is still not hidden
no filtering resolver: private DNS is left alone rather than locked to nothing
developer options allowed: adb survives, and nothing else is loosened with it
developer options allowed together with a resolver: only the debugging entry is missing
uninstalling allowed: apps can be removed, and nothing else is loosened with it
uninstalling allowed while free-installation is off: installing and removing are separate switches
ad filter: a switch and a list url turn the tunnel on
ad filter: the switch alone is not enough — no list url, no tunnel
ad filter: a list url with the switch off filters nothing
ad filter: tracking-only still filters — it is content filtering, not restraint
always-usable apps survive bedtime, a spent quota, a family block, an explicit block and the approval hold
approval without exemption: a LIMIT rule ends the wait, and no rule does not
approval is not exemption: bedtime reaches a LIMIT rule and never an ALLOW
an app's own allowance is spent while the phone still has screen time left
